3.1.value: Interval fund under Rule 23c-3: continuous daily offering at NAV (plus loads where applicable); NO daily redemption. Liquidity is limited to quarterly repurchase offers of between 5% and 25% of outstanding shares at NAV (a fundamental policy changeable only by majority shareholder vote); in practice the Fund expects to offer only the 5% minimum each quarter. Quarterly repurchases occur in March, June, September and December. Shares unlisted; no secondary market expected; 'suitable only for long-term investors.'
3.1.quote: makes quarterly offers to repurchase between 5% and 25% of its outstanding Shares at NAV, pursuant to Rule 23c-3 under the 1940 Act ... it is expected the Fund will offer to repurchase only the minimum amount of 5% of its outstanding Shares.

3.2.value: Mechanics: Board sets Repurchase Offer Amount (5%-25% floor/cap); notice sent 21-42 days before Repurchase Request Deadline; NAV pricing no later than the 14th calendar day after the deadline (in the June 2026 offer, pricing date = deadline, July 9, 2026, period June 5-July 9); payment expected 1-3 business days and no later than 7 calendar days after pricing date. Oversubscription: Fund MAY (not must) buy up to an additional 2% of outstanding shares; beyond that, pro rata allocation, with an odd-lot exception for holders of <100 shares tendering all. Withdrawal/modification allowed until the deadline. Suspension only by Board majority (incl. majority of independent trustees) in four enumerated circumstances.

6.1.quote: The Adviser is a joint venture between affiliates of Ares Management Corporation ... and CION Investment Group, LLC and is controlled by Ares Management.

6.2.value: High complexity, multi-sleeve global credit: >=80% of Managed Assets in directly originated loans, secured floating/fixed syndicated loans, corporate bonds, ABS, CRE loans and other credit instruments (incl. mezzanine, mortgages, distressed); US and European direct lending, high yield, structured credit/CLOs, real estate debt; predominantly below investment grade ('junk') — 'an investment in the Fund should be considered speculative.' Uses leverage (3 revolvers + 12 MRPS series), interest-rate swaps, credit default swaps (buy and sell protection), FX forwards, short sales, PIK income ($88,235K PIK interest+dividends in FY2025), foreign currencies, unfunded commitments.
6.2.section: Principal Investment Strategies; Types of Investments and Related Risks; Notes 6-9
6.2.quote: Credit instruments that are rated below investment grade (commonly referred to as "high yield" securities or "junk bonds") are regarded as having predominantly speculative characteristics ... an investment in the Fund should be considered speculative.

6.3.value: Dual-adviser economics: Adviser (CAM, a CION/Ares JV controlled by Ares) receives 1.25% of Managed Assets + 15% income incentive; it pays Sub-Adviser (Ares Capital Management II) 40% of fees actually received and retained. Disclosed conflicts: trustees/officers hold interests in the Advisers; allocation of investment opportunities and personnel across Ares/CION 'Advised Funds' with overlapping objectives; co-investments with Ares affiliates permitted only per Ares' SEC exemptive order; lack of information barriers; leverage-inclusive fee base rewards leverage; Adviser is its own valuation designee; CAM administration cost reimbursement ($3,995K FY2025); affiliated wholesale marketing agent/dealer manager CION Securities, LLC compensated via dealer manager fee (up to 0.75% within Class A load); expense-support recoupment rights; prospectus states the Fund/Advisers 'do not undertake ... to give advice in a Fiduciary capacity' in connection with the offering.
6.3.source: N-CSR filed 2026-03-06 (Note 3; Letter) and 486BPOS filed 2026-04-29 (Conflicts of Interest), CIK 1678124
6.3.section: Note 3; Conflicts of Interest; Plan of Distribution; fiduciary-capacity disclaimer is in the N-CSR annual report, not the prospectus
6.3.quote: negotiated co-investments may be made only in accordance with the terms of the exemptive order Ares received from the SEC (the "Order") ... which could limit the Fund's ability to participate in a co-investment transaction.

6.4.value: RIC under Subchapter M; fiscal and tax year end December 31; shareholders receive Form 1099-DIV (no K-1). FY2025 distributions characterized 100% ordinary income for tax. Fund pays 4% excise tax on retained excess taxable income ($3,900K accrued FY2025). Repurchase proceeds taxed as capital gain/loss to tendering shareholders. QUALIFIER: capital gain/loss treatment generally applies to shareholders tendering ALL their shares; partial tenders risk deemed-distribution (dividend) treatment.
6.4.source: 486BPOS filed 2026-04-29 and N-CSR filed 2026-03-06 (Note 2, Note 10), CIK 1678124

6.4.quote: As soon as practicable after the end of each calendar year, a statement on Form 1099-DIV identifying the sources of the distributions paid by the Fund to Shareholders for tax purposes will be furnished to Shareholders

6.7.value: Communicability challenge is documented in the filings' own language: the Fund 'is not intended to be a typical traded investment,' is 'suitable only for long-term investors who can bear the risks associated with the limited liquidity of the Shares,' should be 'considered speculative,' and shareholders must understand interval repurchase mechanics, proration risk and NAV fluctuation between tender and pricing. Participant-level communication assessment is downstream.
